test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Motor Vehicle) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In the combustion process, electronically managed fuel injection systems control combustion by:

options.text: controlling the air-fuel ratio using sensors and catalytic converters

solution:
The correct answer is __controlling the air-fuel ratio using sensors and catalytic converters.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Electronically managed fuel injection systems__ play a crucial role in modern combustion processes.
 
• They ensure optimal air-fuel ratios for efficient combustion.
 
• The system uses sensors to monitor engine performance and environmental conditions.
 
• Catalytic converters help reduce emissions by converting harmful gases into less harmful ones.
 
• This technology improves fuel efficiency and reduces environmental impact.
 
• It also minimizes the production of unburnt fuel emissions and maximizes energy extraction.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Combustion Process:**

 
 
• Combustion is the chemical process of burning a fuel source in the presence of oxygen to release energy.
 
• Efficient combustion requires a balanced air-fuel ratio.
 
 
 
• **Fuel Atomisation:**
 
 
• Fuel atomisation refers to breaking fuel into fine droplets for better mixing with air.
 
• This process is crucial for ensuring complete combustion and reducing emissions.
 
 
 
• **Role of Sensors:**
 
 
• Sensors monitor engine conditions like temperature, pressure, and oxygen levels.
 
• They provide real-time data for adjusting the air-fuel ratio.
